title: A reusable turn
introduction: Give a useful sequence a name, then use it twice.
explanation: A function groups commands. Define void turnRight() with three turnLeft(); commands. Calling turnRight(); runs that body and then continues after the call. Definitions alone do not execute.
objective: Follow the U-shaped corridor. Leave one coin on each of its two corners, then reach the far end facing along the last leg. Empty your bag.
instruction: Both worlds use the same distances: four steps, a right turn, two steps, a right turn, four steps. Define and call turnRight().

commands.description: Define a reusable sequence outside main.
Call your function wherever a right turn is needed.

hints: Three left turns equal one right turn.
Place a coin at each corner before continuing.
Define the function once; call it at both corners. The rotated world needs the same relative movements.

illustration.alt: Three left turns produce one right turn. A named function lets the same command sequence be used at both corners.
